questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The Subjects that UVIC offered were very interesting, and opened new oppertunities to try different areas of my study. The location also played a big part. As well as it being an English speaking country

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was amazing!! i recommend it to everyone, even just victoria as a city to visit on Vacation.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: quite easy. you get a Schedule for the International welcome and i suggest you take part in as much as you think is relevant. some of it is very repetetive but you meet the international students who end up becoming your friends.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: They have a Center for internal students on campus who are really sweet and ready to help!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I did not need any help but they were available!

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I knew someone who knew someone, so i was very lucky. but facebook might be the easiest way to find something.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Public transport is not as great as in Copenhagen so look at bus routes before moving somewhere. It is also VERY hilly so biking is a lot tougher than Copenhagen. I lived 20 minutes away by bike or 45 minutes away by bus, but 30 minutes from downtown, which was okay but a little annoying when it took a while to get to and from places.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: housing can be quite expensive, you should budget around 1000$-1600$ per month depending on if you have your own aparment or just rent a room in a house.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A LOT of the courses you see on their current website is not available during the semester and the only way to know this is during the course registration, so! use the "schedule planning" function Asap. i did not have a lot of trouble registrating but some of my friends did, so be aware of your reqruitsites.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: all is online, where you can create a mock schedule and plan it out. You then get a Time slot where you can registrer. this time slot is over 2 weeks so you might be lucky to get an earlier date or a later one, and this also influences if you get on the waiting list for some courses. HOWEVER... it is not impossible to get off the waiting lists as a lot of people drop courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: you can mail the international center (i think) but a lot of people send mails, so it takes some time to get a reply.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was very successfull i got all the courses i wanted. i Also had a very early registration date, so none of the courses were filled up when i registered.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If there is a course you REALLY want, then send en email to the professor directly, they have the power to overwrite the prerqruisites.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I chose a 4th year course which was stupid as i am a 3rd year, as well as it was not a course in my program so it was a thougher new course. i dont recommend it! it was difficult! but i passed, so it is possible.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
I had 1 x 200 Level, 2 x 300 level and 1 x 400 Level. 
the 200-300 were good. the 400 was difficult. 
However... if i had really wanted a good grade in the 400 i could have done it, but i prioriticed other things. 
The level of difficultness in generel i would say is a bit easier than copenhagen, but not so much that you can relax completely.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
there is more lectures, where someone speaks for 1,5 hours and you write notes. There is A LOT of midterm and quizes during the semester that count for 15-25% of your grade, so you dont just have a final exam that counts 100% of your grade. This means also that when you reach the final quiz/project or whatever you already know if you have passed 75% of the course. 
A lot of the finals were online as well. Handing in an online presentation or an essay or a quiz.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: "AE303A Introduction to Ceramics Wheel and Hand Techniques" & "AE307 Printmaking" & "BIOC403 Biochemistry of Signal Transduction" & "ENSH240 Introduction to a Major Author: Taylor Swift"

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
The ceramics was super fun and casual, but requires a lot of extra time and work. This was probably my most demanding course during my semester. Printmaking was also fun but kind of difficult if you cannot draw and it also requires extra time outside of class but not as much as Ceramics. ENSH240 was a phenomenal course, even if you are not a taylor swift fan. The course is analysing lyrics and talking about references to old litterature, poems and songs! (Name redacted) is the best professor i have ever had! so i highly recommend this course! 
BIOC403 was very difficult. and the teacher speaks very fast. i also dont have a background in biochemistry so it was even more difficult. 
I also had "natural hazards" course but dropped it in September. Be aware there are classes with up to 300 people in it. it is not the greatest.

questions.question: Insurance DKK *
Housing DKK per month *
Books DKK per month *
Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *
Communication (phone, internet, etc.) DKK per month *
Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Tipping and taxes are added AFTER the you see the price.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: the groceries are SO expensive. Even more expensive than copenhagen!! so expensive! especially the fruit and vegetable. eating out is also cheaper than CPH. there are a lot of cafes on campus but their stuff is quite expensive. go to the Grad House (even if you are not a Grad student) and get cheap (ish) food there! they also have board games and beer.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They have SO many clubs and other initiatives you can join! it is just about making time for it!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kinds of sports, intermurals, clubs for everyone! check out their list of clubs online.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I found it difficult to find time for all the clubs, but go to the clubs and unions days!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Visit all over the island! Tofino, port alberni, strathcona, campbell river! also the golf islands are amazing for a day trip! Saturna, salt spring, pender and galliano! but you need to rent car! i Went to vancouver for a couple of days and it was Not as cozy and fun as Victoria. I recommend spending all your time on the Island while you are there. as there is so much to see!
Be aware that some things are better during specific months. you can see the salmon jumping in the rivers in November and going to campell river around the same time then you might see a bear grabbing the salmon!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was kind of easy. The small talk is a big change. It is in generel very different but also kind of the same. it is good to talk to other Danes about the experience because it is a little weird, but everyone is very friendly

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Small talk is big, but that does not mean that you are friends. People might say "lets get coffee" but you will not actually get the coffee unless you really arrange it on purpose.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
The small talk, it is very shallow and strange.
There are A LOT of homeless and drug addicts downtown! it was very shocking the first couple of times going downtown after dark, it felt very unsafe. but just try not to be around Pandora Avenue after dark and then nothing will happen, i have not heard of anyone who had a bad experience with the homeless or addicts, so just leave them alone and then they leave you alone.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
The coffee culture. there are many cafes and going for coffee is a big thing! the coffee is cheaper than CPH as well.
How easy it is to start a conversation with random people. people are super interested in talking.
also saying hello and thank you to the bus driver is very nice.
Their thrift stores are REALLY nice! and cheap! so if this is something you like to do in CPH, you can look forward to it in Victoria. i recommend Value village, Broad view united, Beacon hill and WIN. aswell as going to Sydney and brentwood bay they have a lot.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
GET A CREDIT CARD! otherwise you cannot rent a car! and if you want to go on a trip you NEED a car!
The busses only take EXACT cash or UMO buss card! in the first couple of days make sure you have coins on you!
Get Rain pants, Rain coats and Rain boots! IT RAINS!!!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The full time canadian students pay for their buss passes in the tuition but i think 75% of all student have a car, so they dont use it. if you can find a canadian student who havent activated their buss pass you can pay them 50$ or something for it. then you dont have to pay 130$ for it as it costs for international students.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting the people and experiences the nature. The nature is HUGE. you know that before you go but it is crazy to see in real life! it is so beautiful and there are deer everywhere! in the gardens and on campus, everywhere! It was so much fun!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: adjusting to the culture. but after 3 months everything becomes natural, so it is sad to go home after 4 months.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: GO! DO IT! it was so much fun! it was wonderfull and the people were amazing. the food was not the greates but it does not matter. go try all the things you want to do before November/december as it RAINS! it rains so much! 10x as much as Denmark! dont be fooled, i thought it would not be that bad and they were dramatic as we come from a rainy country, But this is on another level! they get asmospheric rivers, which is crazy!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
